title: Walter Shewhart and the Birth of the Control Chart (1924)
explainer: In May 1924, Bell Labs engineer Walter Shewhart wrote a one-page memo introducing the control chart: the first systematic way to separate a process's normal statistical fluctuation ('common cause' variation) from a genuine anomaly ('special cause' variation), using control limits set a fixed number of standard deviations from a baseline. That is the same logic modern observability and AIOps anomaly detection runs on a metric or log stream, and Shewhart's 3-sigma control limits are a direct ancestor of the alerting thresholds engineers tune today.
